count_note: Claims and ownership observations are not unique companies or graph events.

claims.subject: Thompson-Okanagan Transit Ltd.
claims.finding: Formerly Tweed Line Tours Ltd.; a wholly owned subsidiary in the T.S. Holdings consolidation.
claims.limits: The note gives no effective rename date.

claims.subject: Vancouver Island Transit Ltd.
claims.finding: Formerly McArthur Transportation Limited; a wholly owned subsidiary in the T.S. Holdings consolidation.
claims.limits: The note gives no effective rename date. This is distinct from Vancouver Island Transportation Company Limited.

claims.subject: V I T Holdings five-company group
claims.finding: V I T Holdings owns 98.24% of each of the five named companies directly or through a subsidiary.
claims.limits: Snapshot, not an acquisition or percentage-change date; immediate parent unresolved for four of the five.

claims.subject: V I T Holdings five-company group
claims.finding: V I T Holdings owns 98.4% of each of the five named companies directly or through a subsidiary.
claims.limits: Snapshot, not an acquisition or percentage-change date; immediate parent unresolved for four of the five.

claims.subject: V I T Holdings five-company group
claims.finding: V I T Holdings owns 98.5% of each of the five named companies directly or through a subsidiary.
claims.limits: Snapshot, not an acquisition or percentage-change date; immediate parent unresolved for four of the five.

claims.subject: V I T Holdings Ltd. / Vancouver Island Transportation Company Limited
claims.finding: The 1976 and 1977 goodwill notes name V I T Holdings as acquirer of Vancouver Island Transportation; the 1978 note identifies Transportation as its subsidiary; the 1979 note identifies Holdings as seller of the Transportation shareholding.
claims.limits: These statements do not establish the original acquisition date.

claims.subject: Vancouver Island Transportation Company Limited
claims.finding: V I T Holdings sold its 98.5% holding to the Province of British Columbia.
claims.limits: Share transfer, separate from the subsequent asset/liability transaction; not 100%.

claims.subject: V I T Holdings Ltd.
claims.finding: V I T Holdings was liquidated.
claims.limits: The passage does not establish the registry dissolution date.

claims.subject: T.S. Holdings Ltd. subsidiaries
claims.finding: The consolidated wholly owned subsidiary list contains Thompson-Okanagan Transit Ltd. and Vancouver Island Transit Ltd.; subsidiaries sold or liquidated during the year were accounted for to their respective disposal dates.
claims.limits: Do not extend the earlier three-subsidiary observation through 31 March 1979.

claims.subject: Pacific Coach Lines Limited, company 178561
claims.finding: Pacific Coach Lines Limited was incorporated under the British Columbia Companies Act.
claims.limits: The corporate note does not identify the initial shareholder or subscription date.

claims.subject: Pacific Coach Lines Limited, company 178561
claims.finding: Pacific Coach Lines purchased Vancouver Island Transportation Company Limited assets, assumed its liabilities, and commenced operations.
claims.limits: An asset/liability transfer; no legal merger, dissolution, rename or purchase of subsidiaries shares is established.

claims.subject: Pacific Coach Lines Limited, company 178561
claims.finding: Pacific Coach Lines acquired certain assets and operating responsibilities of Pacific Stage Lines, a division of British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority.
claims.limits: This later transfer is not the legal incorporation or first operational start of Pacific Coach.

claims.subject: Pacific Coach Lines Limited, company 178561
claims.finding: The Province held the entire issued capital stock of two common shares.
claims.limits: The schedule confirms the snapshot; it does not by itself date the initial subscription.

claims.subject: T.S. Holdings Ltd.
claims.finding: The Province held the entire issued capital stock of one common share.

claims.subject: Pacific Coach Lines Limited, company 178561
claims.finding: Pacific Coach Lines Limited changed name to 178561 B.C. Ltd.
claims.limits: Publication was 2 August 1990. The notice does not establish ownership in 1990 or a privatization or dissolution date.

claims.subject: Pacific Coach Lines (1984) Ltd., company 273925
claims.finding: The Gazette identifies this separate company as incorporated on 7 February 1984.
claims.limits: No ownership relationship with the original Crown company is established by this notice.

claims.subject: Pacific Coach Lines (1984) Ltd., company 273925
claims.finding: Pacific Coach Lines (1984) Ltd. changed name to 273925 B.C. Ltd.
claims.limits: Publication was 2 August 1990. Distinct legal identity from company 178561.

claims.subject: Royal Victorian Holdings Corporation, company 362538
claims.finding: The Gazette identifies Royal Victorian Holdings Corporation as incorporated on 29 March 1989.
claims.limits: No Crown ownership or acquisition relationship is established by the notice.

claims.subject: Royal Victorian Holdings Corporation, company 362538
claims.finding: Royal Victorian Holdings Corporation changed name to Pacific Coach Lines Ltd.
claims.limits: Publication was 2 August 1990. Distinct legal identity from companies 178561 and 273925.

claims.caution: The notice says amalgamated, not incorporated; this is not the Crown acquisition date.
This proves Hatchery→Surrey Hatchery, not a legal Hatching→Hatchery rename.

claims.scope: Registry identity of the singular-name company; a lead for the sold Housing subsidiary. This notice alone does not prove Ventures plural was an earlier legal name or directly identify its shareholder.

claims.caution: Notice describes the company’s incorporation date, not necessarily its original incorporated name.
The dated note supports full names and group membership; it supplies no registry-number bridge to Statistics Canada’s shortened variants.

claims.upper_bound_basis: Authenticated Food Exhibitions name used in auditor report dated17 June 1985, for financial statements as at 31 March 1985.
claims.caution: Archive coverage gaps and negative OCR searches do not narrow the legal rename to March–June 1985. 1980–1983 were not comprehensively searched.

claims.statement: Original OIC 631/1986, approved 19 March 1986, brings the Repeal Act into force effective 31 March 1986. Section 2 dissolves the company on repeal. The official consolidation identifies B.C. Reg. 49/86.
claims.reasoning: Legal endpoint follows the explicit dissolution-on-repeal clause applied to the effective date in the recovered original commencement order.

claims.statement: The 1985/86 Public Accounts separately state dissolution and transfer effective 1 April 1986, while acknowledging Act commencement on 31 March.
claims.confidence: high that the Accounts print this assertion
claims.treatment: Retain as an attributed assertion alongside the recommended legal endpoint; do not silently normalize the documents or claim a proven typographical error.
claims.unresolved: The reason for the Accounts' next-day dissolution wording remains unexplained. The original order now establishes legal commencement on 31 March 1986.

claims.statement: BC Cellulose acquired 79% on 29 June 1973; the same percentage is observed at 31 December 1975.
claims.graph_recommendation: Separate majority-controlled subsidiary record; do not classify as wholly provincially owned. Public acquisition is not incorporation.

claims.statement: The 1973 transaction combined certain Columbia Cellulose assets and liabilities with Canadian Cellulose, after which Columbia ceased to be its shareholder.
claims.graph_recommendation: Do not collapse these into one entity or model the transaction as a simple rename.

claims.statement: All shares were purchased by BC Cellulose effective 1 March 1974 from Eddy Match; the company also acquired assets and third-party liabilities of Eddy Match operating divisions.
claims.graph_recommendation: Add a wholly owned subsidiary from this public acquisition date; keep incorporation unresolved and do not duplicate the same-named acquired division.
claims.related_accounting_date_note: Parent F7 measures goodwill/equity at acquisition on 28 February; use subsidiary explicit 1 March effective purchase date for the ownership event.

claims.entity: Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited; Kootenay Forest Products Ltd.; Plateau Mills Ltd.
claims.statement: BC Cellulose distributed these securities to the Province before transfer to BCRIC. The precise dividend date remains unknown.
claims.date_bounds_basis: Inferred from fiscal-year 1977/78 transactions and the completed BCRIC transfer on 9 March 1978.
claims.confidence: high for transaction, moderate for inferred bounds
claims.graph_recommendation: Preserve the Province as an intermediate direct owner with a bounded start; do not invent an exact dividend date.

claims.statement: The Province combined 9,570,353 common and 39,750 non-voting shares received from BC Cellulose with 278,100 common shares held separately as a temporary investment. The combined interest transferred to BCRIC was 81%.
claims.graph_recommendation: Retain 79% as BC Cellulose historical holding and 81% as the combined Province/BCRIC transfer observation; do not backdate 81% to the holding-company acquisition.

claims.entity: Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited; Kootenay Forest Products Ltd.; Plateau Mills Ltd.
claims.statement: The Finance Minister reported the actual transfer to BCRIC on 9 March 1978, with holdings of 81%, 100% and 100% respectively.
claims.locator: Hansard 10 April 1978 afternoon, p.264; OIC 530/1978 PDF 1,3–4
claims.evidence_boundary: Hansard provides retrospective completion evidence; the OIC alone supplies approval and agreement date.

claims.entity: British Columbia Resources Investment Corporation and its subsidiaries
claims.statement: The public share issue and Crown note conversion occurred in calendar 1979. The Accounts describe the government interest falling from 100% to below 5%; the exact day of crossing the control threshold is unresolved.
claims.date_bounds_basis: Subsequent-events narrative after the March 1979 accounts plus BCRIC audited comparative cash flows explicitly placing the public cash issue and note conversion in calendar 1979.
claims.confidence: high for year; exact day unresolved
claims.graph_recommendation: End wholly/majority provincial classification at year precision 1979; do not use 1980 amalgamation as public-control endpoint. Retain later minority Crown interest if modeled.

claims.statement: BCRIC increased its ownership from 81% to 100% during 1980, after the 1979 public issue.
claims.locator: p2 / PDF 4; p23 / PDF 25 note 2 continuation
claims.graph_recommendation: Do not describe this as 100% provincial ownership. BCRIC ownership and ultimate Crown ownership differ.

claims.entity: Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited; Kootenay Forest Products Ltd.; Plateau Mills Ltd.
claims.statement: The three companies amalgamated on 31 December 1980 into a new Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited.
claims.graph_recommendation: Record the successor event separately from public-control cessation; do not call it a BC Cellulose rename or infer operational closure.

claims.entity: Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited; Kootenay Forest Products Ltd.
claims.statement: Original incorporation dates were not established in this pass. The recovered exact beginnings are public acquisition dates.
claims.graph_recommendation: Leave incorporation unknown or use separately sourced prior incorporation evidence. Do not promote acquisition dates into legal formation dates.

claims.subject: Swan Valley Foods federal legal-history lead
claims.limits: Post-sale legal history; not original incorporation or full-public-ownership acquisition. Provincial registry-number bridge remains a separate identity task.
